evidence.paraphrase: The world has eliminated many longstanding social ills.
evidence.quote:
There were no prisons, no slums, no insane asylums, no cripples, no
poverty, no wars.

evidence.paraphrase: Disease and aging have been cured.
evidence.quote: All diseases were conquered. So was old age.

evidence.paraphrase: Death now occurs only by accident or voluntary choice.
evidence.quote: Death, barring accidents, was an adventure for volunteers.

evidence.paraphrase: The national population is held fixed at forty million.
evidence.quote:
The population of the United States was stabilized at forty-million
souls.

evidence.paraphrase: Births have become rare as a consequence of population control.
evidence.quote:
He was the only man
waiting. Not many people were born a day any more.

evidence.paraphrase: Human lifespans are drastically extended, making 56 young.
evidence.quote:
Wehling was fifty-six, a mere stripling in a population whose average
age was one hundred and twenty-nine.

evidence.paraphrase: Medical imaging revealed the pregnancy was triplets.
evidence.quote: X-rays had revealed that his wife was going to have triplets.

evidence.paraphrase: An old man is roughly two hundred years old.
evidence.quote: about two hundred years old, sat on a stepladder

evidence.paraphrase: A cure for aging exists that halts further aging.
evidence.quote:
Aging had
touched him that much before the cure for aging was found.

evidence.paraphrase: A government agency exists to manage terminations.
evidence.quote:
the Chicago Office of the Federal Bureau of
Termination

evidence.paraphrase: The painter contrasts the idealized mural with real life.
evidence.quote:
"You think this is my idea of what life really looks
like?"

evidence.paraphrase: A phone number connects citizens to state-run gas chambers.
evidence.quote:
"To be or not to be" was the telephone number of the municipal gas
chambers of the Federal Bureau of Termination.

evidence.paraphrase: The painter voices disdain for the orderly society.
evidence.quote:
"The world could do with a good deal more
mess, if you ask me," he said.

evidence.paraphrase: Gas-chamber hostesses reportedly grow mustaches over time.
evidence.quote:
they all sprouted mustaches
within five years or so.

evidence.paraphrase: Leora admires Hitz for founding the first local gas chamber.
evidence.quote:
"He was
responsible for setting up the very first gas chamber in Chicago."

evidence.paraphrase: Law requires a volunteer death for each new birth.
evidence.quote:
The law said that no newborn child could survive unless the parents of
the child could find someone who would volunteer to die.

evidence.paraphrase: Wehling bitterly describes having to choose which child lives.
evidence.quote:
All I have to do is pick
out which one of the triplets is going to live, then deliver my maternal
grandfather to the Happy Hooligan

evidence.paraphrase: Hitz cites runaway population growth that prompted control.
evidence.quote:
Would you like to go back to the good old days, when the population of
the Earth was twenty billion--about to become forty billion, then eighty
billion, then one hundred and sixty billion?

evidence.paraphrase: Hitz explains overcrowding via a blackberry analogy.
evidence.quote:
"A drupelet, Mr. Wehling, is one of the little knobs, one of the little
pulpy grains of a blackberry,"

evidence.paraphrase: Past overpopulation caused water and food shortages until scientists intervened.
evidence.quote:
In the year 2000," said Dr. Hitz, "before scientists stepped in and
laid down the law, there wasn't even enough drinking water to go around,
and nothing to eat but sea-weed

evidence.paraphrase: Wehling states he wants to keep all three children.
evidence.quote: "I want those kids," said Wehling quietly. "I want all three of them."

evidence.paraphrase: Euphemistic official naming contrasts with the grim reality of state killing.
evidence.quote:
He corrected
himself, gave the municipal gas chambers their official title, a title
no one ever used in conversation. "I should have said, 'Ethical Suicide
Studios,'"

evidence.paraphrase: Wehling murders Hitz to make room for a child.
evidence.quote:
Wehling shot Dr. Hitz dead. "There's room for one--a great big one," he
said.

evidence.paraphrase: Wehling kills himself and Duncan to free space for his triplets.
evidence.quote: And then he shot himself, making room for all three of his children.

evidence.paraphrase: The painter reflects on the fundamental problem of reproduction on a finite planet.
evidence.quote:
The painter pondered the mournful puzzle of life demanding to be born
and, once born, demanding to be fruitful ... to multiply and to live as
long as possible--to do all that on a very small planet that would have
to last forever.

evidence.paraphrase: The painter decides to stop painting after the killings.
evidence.quote: He knew that he would never paint again.

evidence.paraphrase: The painter tries but cannot shoot himself.
evidence.quote:
He took Wehling's pistol, really intending to shoot himself.

But he didn't have the nerve.

evidence.paraphrase: The termination hostess frames suicide as a civic gift to the future.
evidence.quote:
"Your city thanks you; your country
thanks you; your planet thanks you. But the deepest thanks of all is
from future generations."
